title: Law Firm Marketing and Professional Services | 22 Signals
description: Law firm marketing, websites, client portals and AI intake for law firms, consultancies and accountants. Get named in Google and in AI answers.
h1: Law firm marketing and growth for professional services firms
intro: 22 Signals handles law firm marketing and growth for law firms, consultancies and accounting practices, mostly in the US. People now ask Google, ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini which firm to call. We build the websites, search presence, content, client portals and AI intake that get a firm named in those answers and turn inquiries into signed clients.

sections.h: How clients choose a firm now
p: A person injured in a crash, a founder looking for a fractional finance team, a family business needing a new accountant: each of them starts with a search or a question to an AI assistant. The firms that get the call are the ones that appear in the first answers, look credible when the prospect clicks, and respond before the next firm does.

Most firms are strong on the work and weak on those three steps. The website is out of date, the content is generic, and inquiries wait in a shared inbox. We fix the whole chain, from the first search to the signed engagement letter.

p: We produce monthly SEO and content for US personal injury firms, and every statute is checked. That means the statute of limitations is right for the state, the comparative fault rule is correct, and a page about a local road or court names the right one. A wrong number on a legal page is worse than no page at all.

Each piece follows the same process: research, a draft written to answer the searcher's question in the first lines, a legal fact check, then review by the firm. The firm keeps final approval on everything that carries its name.

For a US law firm we built a client portal where clients upload documents, track their matter and pay invoices in one place. It replaces the back-and-forth of emailed attachments and gives the firm one record of what each client had sent.

Law firm websites are also a target. We have cleaned up compromised law firm sites: removing injected spam pages and malicious code, closing the hole that let it in, recovering search listings and putting monitoring and updates in place so it does not happen again. Every site we build or take over gets security care as standard.

Right now, 10 of the businesses we work with sit in Google's top five for their main searches and show up in ChatGPT's answers. For firms, that comes from consistent practice-area pages, accurate directory and bar profiles, real reviews and outside mentions, maintained month after month rather than in a single push.

For consultancies and accountants the buyer is usually a business, and the sale is slower. Search still matters, but so do positioning, a clear offer and a steady flow of conversations. We help firms define who they serve and what they sell, then build the content, LinkedIn presence and outbound system to reach those buyers.

Inside the firm, we automate the repetitive work: onboarding checklists, document collection, engagement letters, recurring reports and dashboards that show utilization and pipeline. AI tools can draft first versions of routine documents for a professional to review, with client data kept within agreed systems.

Every page, video and ad avoids misleading claims and promises about outcomes. For US firms we work within the state bar advertising rules the firm follows, including disclaimers where required. For UK firms we keep to SRA guidance and the UK GDPR when handling client data. Your firm keeps final approval on everything we publish.

We follow Talk, Plan, Build, Grow. One Signal Lead runs your account across search, web, content and intake, and every deliverable has a date in writing. Monthly reports show rankings, inquiries, calls and signed cases or engagements where your systems allow us to track them.
Cost depends on scope: the number of practice areas and office locations, how much content you need each month, whether we are rebuilding the website or a portal, and whether we manage paid search.

faqs.q: How do law firms show up in ChatGPT's answers?
faqs.a: By being described clearly and consistently across the sources assistants read. That includes the firm's own practice-area pages, but also reviews, legal directories, bar profiles, local news and lists. Firms with accurate, consistent information across those sources, strong reviews and pages that answer real client questions get named more often.

faqs.q: Can we change our domain or rebuild our site without losing rankings?
faqs.a: Yes, if the migration is planned properly. We build a full redirect map, keep content parity for pages that rank, update directory listings and Google Business Profile, and monitor rankings and errors after launch. Most ranking losses after a rebuild come from missing redirects and deleted pages.

faqs.q: Does your AI intake give legal advice?
faqs.a: No. The assistant answers routine questions such as office hours, practice areas and what to bring to a consultation, collects the prospect's details and books a time. Anything that sounds like a request for legal advice is handed to a person at the firm. We agree those rules with you and test them before launch.

faqs.q: Who checks the legal accuracy of your content?
faqs.a: Our writers research every statute, deadline and court reference against primary sources before a draft goes to the firm. The firm then reviews and approves it. We never publish legal content without the firm's sign-off, and we update pages when the law changes.

faqs.q: Our website was hacked. Can you fix it?
faqs.a: Yes. We have cleaned up compromised law firm websites. We remove malicious code and spam pages, close the vulnerability, request removal of spam URLs from search results, restore clean backups where needed and set up updates and monitoring. Then we check that rankings and listings recover.

faqs.q: Do you work with UK law firms as well as US firms?
faqs.a: Yes. Our head office is in London and we work with UK firms on websites, search, content and intake. UK pages follow SRA guidance, use British spelling and legal terms, and handle client data under the UK GDPR. Most of our legal content work today is for US personal injury firms, so UK projects start with a short review of your market.

faqs.q: Do you work with accountants and consultancies too?
faqs.a: Yes. For accounting practices and consultancies we focus on positioning, search, LinkedIn and outbound to reach business buyers, and on automating internal work such as onboarding, document collection and recurring reports. The same one-lead model applies.

faqs.q: What does law firm marketing with 22 Signals cost?
faqs.a: It depends on scope. The main factors are the number of practice areas and locations, monthly content volume, whether you need a new website or client portal, and whether we run paid search. We send a written scope with dates after a 15-minute call.
